study: Worth et al. 2017 (Teacher Observation, EEF/NFER cluster RCT)
delivery_evidence: CMPO researchers gave face-to-face training to lead teachers (a day's training: introducing the rubric, installing the TOWER app on tablets, exploring the software together); lead teachers then cascaded training in-school via formal/informal meetings (some written information). No online/remote training delivery -- the tablet software is the PD's subject, not its delivery channel (p.~9/35 'CMPO researchers trained lead teachers...'; Implementation p.~40).
test_alignment_evidence: Outcomes are national GCSE point scores (combined English+maths composite, and the English/maths subscales) -- a broad independent high-stakes examination not tailored to the intervention (extraction test_type=standardized_independent; Table 13 p.31).
curriculum_evidence: Intervention is a structured peer-observation PROCESS using RANDA TOWER software/rubric to improve teacher effectiveness; no new curriculum, textbook, or student-facing instructional materials are adopted -- teachers continue normal teaching (Exec summary p.~9 'improve teacher effectiveness through structured peer observation').
outcome_timing_evidence: Primary contrast = Cohort 2 GCSE (2016), taken at the end of the two-year intervention (Year 11); the extracted end-of-treatment full-exposure wave, no post-treatment follow-up (extraction timepoint 'post (2016 GCSE; end of two-year intervention)', Table 13 p.31).
